report_name: Critical Flaws in Elecbrakes Allow Remote Brake Hijacking

attack_patterns.name: Wireless Compromise
attack_patterns.description: An unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range can connect to the Elecbrakes controller due to a lack of proper authentication in the BLE protocol.

attack_patterns.name: Manipulation of Control
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can send malicious commands to the brake controller to remotely engage or disengage a trailer's brakes, creating a physical safety risk.

attack_patterns.name: System Firmware
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can flash the controller with malicious firmware due to an insecure update mechanism, allowing for persistent control over the braking system.

attack_patterns.name: Network Sniffing
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can capture legitimate braking commands sent over the Bluetooth Low Energy protocol to perform a replay attack.

tools.name: gatttool
tools.description: A command-line tool used for interacting with Bluetooth Low Energy devices, which can be used to scan for and send malicious commands to vulnerable Elecbrakes controllers.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Authentication in Elecbrakes BLE Protocol
vulnerabilities.description: The Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication between the Elecbrakes control unit and the smartphone app or remote lacks proper authentication, allowing any nearby device to connect and send commands.

vulnerabilities.name: Replay Attack Vulnerability in Elecbrakes BLE Protocol
vulnerabilities.description: The communication protocol is vulnerable to replay attacks, allowing an attacker to capture and replay legitimate braking commands to trigger actions such as sudden braking without driver input.

vulnerabilities.name: Insecure Firmware Update Mechanism in Elecbrakes Controllers
vulnerabilities.description: The firmware update process lacks sufficient validation, potentially allowing an attacker to flash the controller with malicious firmware for persistent control.

identities.name: Elecbrakes
identities.description: Australian manufacturer of the vulnerable Bluetooth-enabled trailer brake controllers (EB2, VM1, ELBC 2000).

identities.name: Element Digital
identities.description: Security consultancy that discovered and reported the vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes devices.

identities.name: CISA
identities.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which issued an advisory on the Elecbrakes vulnerabilities.
